passages.note: Third Reading roll call shows Carter voting Y on HB2492, a single-subject citizenship-verification bill, with a 31-26-3-0-0 tally well below near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship.
passages.note: HB2492's enacted text requires satisfactory evidence of citizenship to complete voter registration, matching rung 5's documentary-proof clause.
Bill status page lists Carter as a co-sponsor of HB2492, the citizenship-verification registration bill signed into law 2022-03-30.

rows.reasoning: Carter co-sponsored and voted Y on HB 2492 (2022), a single-subject Arizona bill whose operative text requires that registration applications 'be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship' and directs rejection of applications lacking it, matching the rung text 'Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote.' The vote tally of 31-26-3-0-0 is well below the near-unanimous threshold, and both his sponsorship and his in-chamber vote during his State Representative service support this chair.
